topics.witness: Initial: empty store. Owner creates project A (entry #1). The same day, the owner, confirming, erases audit entries before a date earlier than every entry's instant, so nothing qualifies and nothing is removed. Outcome 1: an erasure entry #2 naming the date and carrying a confirmation id. This is forced by [q:R0-66.text] and [q:R0-66.row] (the erasure leaves an entry of its own whatever it removed), [q:M09.erasure_writes] and [q:M09.conf]/[q:R0-37.audit] (the id where the owner confirmed). Outcome 2: no entry and no id. This is forced by V4's A15 rule 6, which the version table says still wrote nothing for an empty erasure until V5 reversed it, and by [q:A14.r5.old] (a confirmed action that changes nothing mints none), which was in force until b31d9eac.
topics.observer: the owner reading the log in the periodic review (whether the erasure left its trace, and with which confirmation id)
topics.needed: nothing (V4's verbatim A15 rule 6 and A14 rule 3 would only confirm what the version table summarises)
topics.why: At V4 the State 2 rules make an empty erasure write nothing and mint nothing, while R0-66 and M09 require its own entry with an id. The two give observably different logs.

topics.witness: Initial: empty store. Owner creates A (#1). The same day, the owner, confirming, erases before a date older than every entry. Expected on V5: entry #2 naming the date. [q:A14.r3.new] names the erasure as the exception to 'changes nothing writes nothing', [q:A15.r6.new] says it writes its entry 'whatever it removed' as 'the one accepted action that writes an entry without changing other state', and [q:A14.inv.new] admits 'a an erasure of old entries'.
topics.observer: nobody (the entry is written under either label; only the formal classification differs)
topics.why: V5 handles the entry side explicitly as an exception (A14 r3 new, A15 r6 new, A14 invariant new). Whether the entry itself counts as a 'change' does not alter whether it is written.

topics.witness: Initial: empty store. Owner creates A (#1). The same day, the owner, confirming, erases before a date older than every entry. Outcome 1: entry #2 carries a freshly minted confirmation id, forced by [q:A15.r6.new] ('with its confirmation id') and [q:M09.conf]. Outcome 2: no id is minted, forced by [q:A14.r5.old] ('a confirmed action that changes nothing mints none'), which was still in force at V5 (replaced only at b31d9eac), on the default reading that the erasure's own entry is not a change of state.
topics.observer: the owner reading the log (whether the erasure entry answers to a confirmation id)
topics.why: At V5, A15 r6 was reversed but A14 r5 still excluded no-change confirmed actions from minting. The texts conflict unless the erasure's own entry counts as a state change, which the packet says is not the default reading. V6's A14 r5 new fixes this.

topics.witness: Initial: empty store. Day 1: owner creates A (entry #1, written in the create's transaction). Day 2: the owner, confirming, erases before day 2, so #1 is removed and erasure entry #2 is written. Read over the log as it now stands, the right-to-left direction of [q:A14.inv.new] fails, because the accepted create has no existing entry. Read at the action's transaction ([q:A14.r1] 'in the same transaction'), it holds. A restore makes the same point. Every observable log is identical under both readings.
topics.observer: nobody (only a test generated literally from the formula would fail on a correct implementation)
topics.why: The packet's section 6 states that no behaviour differs. Erasure by [q:A15.r1]/[q:A15.r3] legitimately removes entries, so the invariant is satisfiable only when read at the transaction.
